title: Cardiovirus Coverage Audit
standfirst: Cardiovirus holds encephalomyocarditis virus (Cardiovirus A, C. rueckerti), Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus (Cardiovirus B, C. theileri) and Saffold virus (Cardiovirus D, C. saffoldi), the one of the three isolated from humans. Theiler's virus is also the standard animal model of multiple sclerosis. This audit covers the module built for the genus: what it covers, how it was built, where the cutoffs sit, whether genomes reach it, whether it calls the proteins, and what it cannot do.
headline_tiles: vocabulary collapse at equal proteins sampled

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: One genus, one layout, thirteen features — and two proteins the layout does not describe.

blocks.html: The cardiovirus polyprotein is leader, VP4, VP2, VP3, VP1, 2A, 2B, 2C, 3A, VPg, 3C, 3D. The leader is a 67–76 residue zinc-finger protein, median 71, that antagonises host nucleocytoplasmic trafficking, not a protease: it is a different protein from the 201-residue aphthovirus leader protease that occupies the same slot, which is why the two genera are separate modules.

rows: genomes in the BV-BRC protein dump

blocks.html: Two further proteins are made from the same RNA and are not in the module. L* is translated from an alternative AUG in the leader region, out of frame with the polyprotein. 2B* is a transframe fusion made by ribosomal frameshifting inside 2B. Both are well attested, and section 07 reports what this module does about them, which is nothing yet.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: Thirteen features at the documented defaults, 60 profiles.

blocks.html: Every collection was large enough to build at -m 5 -mi 0.8. The thinnest are VPg at 22 sequences and 3A at 36, which still cleared the floor, so no feature needed a departure and no cut site had to be projected from polyproteins.

sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit
sections.lede: Windows at 0.8× to 1.2× the collection median, bit cutoffs at 0.45× the median length with a floor of 20.

blocks.html: Self-recall against each feature's own in-range collection: 1083 of 1086 (99.7%) — POLY 106/106, Ldr 69/69, VP4 45/47, VP2 101/101, VP3 87/87, VP1 126/126, 2A 101/101, 2B 82/83, 2C 107/107, 3A 36/36, VPG 22/22, 3C 92/92, 3D 109/109. This is a floor, not a validation; the held-out figures are in §05 and §06.

sections.title: Does it route?
sections.lede: Fifteen rep contigs, and every exemplar routes.

rows: genomes ≥ 5 kb, clustered at 95% nucleotide identity

blocks.html: 15 rep contigs ship with the module; 15 of them are the best BLASTn hit for at least one exemplar. Routing was measured against the ten Picornaviridae modules only — nucleotide BLASTn cannot reach the routing threshold across virus families, and leaving the other 56 modules' 558 rep contigs out cut the run time four-fold.

sections.title: Does it call the proteins?
sections.lede: Every core protein on at least 97 of 106 exemplars, and no feature trails the best by 20 points.

blocks.html: 93 of 106 routed exemplars get every declared feature. No core feature trails the best-called one by 20 points or more.

The lowest are VPg at 97, and 2A and 3A at 98. VPg is 22 residues, so it sits on the 20-bit floor where the length window does most of the discrimination; the nine genomes that miss it are not concentrated in any one species. The leader is called on 101, which for a protein this short and this variable across the genus is the expected shape rather than a coverage hole.

sections.title: Are the calls right?
sections.lede: 40 of 40 held-out genomes clean, with no flag of any kind.

blocks.html: The panel is 40 genomes drawn round-robin across species from this genus's own BV-BRC contigs, with every rep-contig reference genome excluded, built into GTOs with rast-create-genome and scored by viral_genome_quality.pl. Genuinely clean means no genome, contig or feature flag at all.

The panel is 40 genomes drawn round-robin across species from the genus's own BV-BRC contigs, with every rep-contig reference genome excluded, built into GTOs with rast-create-genome and scored by viral_genome_quality.pl. No genome, contig or feature flag fired on any of them. This is the cleanest panel of the ten picornavirus modules.

sections.title: What it cannot do
sections.lede: Two proteins the module does not call, both proven, both measurable in this data.

blocks.html: L* is not a feature. Theiler's virus translates L* from an alternative AUG in the leader coding region, out of frame with the polyprotein; virus carrying a mutated L* start has sharply reduced demyelinating activity (Chen et al. 1995, PMID 7585219; the alternative initiation site was mapped by Kong & Roos 1991, PMID 2033677). Searching the 106 routed exemplars for an ORF of 100 codons or more, starting at an AUG within 150 nucleotides of the polyprotein start and in a different frame, finds one in 41 of them — 23 C. theileri, 6 C. ranori, 4 rodent cardioviruses, and singletons elsewhere. Median length 156 residues. The protein is there and the module does not name it.

2B* is not a feature. Encephalomyocarditis virus makes a 128–129 residue transframe protein by −1 ribosomal frameshifting at a conserved G_GUU_UUY motif shortly after the 2A/2B junction; knocking it out gives a small-plaque phenotype (Loughran et al. 2011, PMID 22025686). Theiler's virus uses the same site at an efficiency of 74–82%, the highest recorded for any virus, into a much shorter ORF (Finch et al. 2015, PMID 26063423). Reading the motif at its correct codon phase in the 106 exemplars finds it in-frame and intact in 21, all of them C. rueckerti, and the resulting construct translates to 128–130 residues in every one — a match to the published length that was not fitted to it. The theilovirus genomes carry the motif too, 16 nucleotides before the called 2B start.

Neither is a threshold problem and neither is a profile problem. L* needs a collection and a normal PSSM feature, since an overlapping ORF in another frame is still found by tblastn. 2B* needs special: transcript_edit and a per-genome nucleotide reference set, because it is not collinear with the genome. Both are work orders, not mysteries: the sequences are extracted and counted above. Neither has been built.

The module calls all thirteen polyprotein products reliably and calls neither of the genus's two out-of-frame proteins. That is a real gap of known size — 41 L* ORFs and 21 EMCV 2B* constructs in 106 exemplars — and it is the next work on this module.

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: Nothing needed fixing, and that is itself the finding.

blocks.html: Full-taxon coverage and the held-out panel were both run for the first time on 4 October 2026. Coverage routed every exemplar, no feature trailed its neighbours by 20 points, and the panel returned no flags, so steps 13 and 14 had nothing to chase. The module was built on 2 October and has not been rebuilt.

What the run did surface is what the earlier steps are structurally unable to see: two proteins that are absent from the module's own feature list. No measurement of how well the declared features perform can report a protein that was never declared. Finding them took reading the genus's literature and then going back to the sequence to check, which is section 07.

sections.title: What the vocabulary bought
sections.lede: Seventy ways of writing thirteen proteins.

blocks.html: Rarefaction over proteins: every annotated protein in the 105 genomes both sources annotate (818 source product records, 1,333 module calls) shuffled 100 times and drawn one at a time. Both curves start at zero. The source vocabulary reaches 70 distinct strings, the module's 13. At the depth both reach, 818 proteins, free text has used 70.0 strings against 13.0 — a 5.4-fold difference. The source reaches 95% of its final size after 711 proteins, the module after 38.

Cardiovirus is better annotated than the duck or porcine genera and correspondingly more inconsistent: 97 distinct source strings collapse into 14 controlled ones. Drawn one protein at a time, the source vocabulary needs 711 of its 818 records to reach 95% of its final 70 strings and is still rising at the end; the module reaches 95% of its 13 after 38 proteins and adds nothing after that.

Nineteen source strings bind to no feature, and the two groups of them say different things. Most are ordinary names — polyprotein (36 records), protein 2A, capsid protein VP1 — that do match a rule but whose sequences were then dropped by the length and ambiguity filters, so they reach no collection. collect_synmap.py reads collection membership rather than rule matches, so a filtered record is indistinguishable here from an unmatched one; the count is a lower bound on what the vocabulary binds. The other group is not an artefact: five distinct strings name L* (L* protein, protein L*, L* peptide, L*) and one names protein 2B*. Those reach no collection because the module declares no such feature — the source data naming the two proteins section 07 says the module does not call.
